objectClass.notes: One 3.0 m module of a plain uncaged steel escape ladder (no hoops, no cage bars -- rebuilt 2026-08-28 with the cage removed), cut flat at both ends so a builder stacks N of them up a wall. Nothing on it turns, opens or swings; nothing attaches to it -- the next segment is placed at +3.0 m, not socketed. One root pivot at back-center on the wall plane, zero sockets. Back and side walls of Bangkok shophouses, walk-ups and small office blocks; stacks in 3.0 m steps to any parapet. Pale grey paint dulled and chalking, rust at every weld and nut, galvanised bolt plates cleaner than the ladder.

reasoning: ONE frame merge on one material -- two flat-bar stiles and one bracket pair (two standoff arms, two gussets, two galvanised wall plates, six bolt heads) -- plus ONE InstancedMesh of ten rungs (rod, two rust weld sleeves, two brass nuts): TWO draw calls of 4.
One material: painted steel as vertex colours on white -- pale blue-grey paint, galvanised plate, silver bolt, brass nut, rust-brown sleeve -- with a sparse rust-bloom multiply canvas.
Repetition system: the rung is the one part repeated at a fixed pitch (ten at 0.30 m), so it is a single instanced geometry.
Action readiness: one root pivot, zero sockets, one box collider on the root, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The identity is the module contract -- stile spacing, rung pitch, bracket at the bottom edge only -- read off the registry notes, dressed in the plate's detail: chunky flat-bar stiles, round rungs with brass nuts on the stile faces, galvanised plates with three bolts, blue-grey paint rusting at the welds.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 0.70 x 3.00 x 0.26 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=2000 triangles, <=4 draw calls, <=2 materials, <=4 unique geometries.

Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

pivotInventory.justification: The rigid body of the prop at its declared origin. A named pivot is a promise that a part turns on it, and only real mechanisms get one.

actionReadiness.socketJustification: ZERO sockets, deliberately. Nothing attaches to this prop and nothing is emitted from it. A marker named for a place on the surface is a location, not a mechanism.

colliderInventory.note: Declared on the asset as box: the ladder envelope from the wall plane to the stile fronts, which is what a stacked run collides as.

actionReadiness.destructionJustification: The asset declares destructionGroups as an empty list -- this prop is NOT breakable. No component carries actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup. promote-model checks built against declared as an equality in BOTH directions, so an invented group fails the gate just as a missing one would.

coordinateFrame.notes: Origin back-center on the WALL PLANE at the bottom edge, +Y up, +Z away from the wall (the climbing face). The next segment sits at +3.0 m on Y with the same wall alignment.

silhouette.description: A 0.70 m wide, 3.00 m tall, 0.26 m deep flat ladder: two flat-bar stiles 0.45 m apart standing 0.20 m off the wall, ten round rungs at 0.30 m pitch from 0.15 m, and at the bottom edge one bracket pair reaching back to two bolt plates on the wall plane, outboard of the stiles. No cage.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x spans -0.340..+0.340 at the outer edges of the 100 mm wall plates centred at +-0.29 (0.68 m built against 0.70 declared, 3% inside the 5% tolerance); y 0.00 to 3.00, the stiles cut flat at both ends; z 0.000 at the wall-plate backs to 0.260 at the stile fronts (stiles stand 0.20 m off the wall on the brackets, 60 mm deep). Depth was 0.85 m to the outside of a safety cage until 2026-08-28, when the registry dropped the cage; with no cage the deepest element is the stile. The plate is a two-rung stand-in of a short section (its prompt asked for stiles, rungs and bolt plates and no lattice), and the proxy reads it at w/h 0.614, d/h 0.113 with plates at both ends: scaled by the 0.45 m stile spacing (61 of 80 columns = 0.76 W) that is a 0.65 x 1.06 x 0.12 m section with rungs at a 0.49 m pitch -- the plate's proportions are a stand-in, not the asset. The DECLARED 0.70 x 3.00 x 0.26 with ten rungs at 0.30 m is the registry's stacking contract and is what is built, so the band table's width residual (0.614 vs 0.233 H) is the declared aspect, not a build error.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate: 1,742 triangles, bbox w/h 0.614 d/h 0.113, occupancy map (scratch/_mon/occupancy.mjs) reading two rungs at 0.26-0.30 H and 0.72-0.76 H, stiles 4 of 80 columns wide, bolt plates at both ends 0.80-0.98 H and 0.00-0.14 H, 10 columns wide. Used for the stile section, rung diameter and plate proportions; NOT for length or counts, which the notes fix. The band table's width residual is the declared aspect (arithmetic in envelopeDerivation), not a build error; with the cage gone the candidate is wider than deep, like the plate, and the depth row agrees.

viewEvidence.note: NOT DIRECTLY OBSERVED. Confidence 0.90: the wall side is the bracket arms and plate backs, which the notes fix; the plate shows the plates from the front with their bolts.

pivot.name: root
pivot.notes: At the origin the asset declares. A STATIC prop: nothing opens, turns or swings, so one root pivot is the whole mechanism inventory and that is the correct answer, not a gap.

collider.notes: Declared on the asset as box: the ladder envelope from the wall plane to the stile fronts, which is what a stacked run collides as.

roughness.notes: Scalar observed for this surface in the plate. The independently extracted map is kept on disk as evidence and is NOT bound at runtime -- this material is textureless, so the scalar is the runtime value.

albedo.samplingNotes: Measured as the mean of crops/paint.png. extract_pbr_evidence confidence 0.860. The extractor palette is advisory only: these crops are flat material swatches, not isolated objects, so its foreground separation is weak by its own warnings. Albedo is the direct crop measurement.

localOverrides.region: rung-to-stile welds and the bolt plates
localOverrides.evidence: crops/rust.png -- orange rust at the welds and streaking below the plates; carried as sleeves at the rung ends plus a sparse bloom tile.

evidence: Measured on viewEvidence region-paint (0.88) at #b2c2c7 sd 21 (pale blue-grey paint) and region-rung at #bdbeb7; carried at #b2c2c7 as vertex colour on a WHITE material; wall plates #d0d4d2 off region-plate #cfd3d0; bolt heads #c4c6c8 off region-bolt; nuts #b08a3c off region-nut; weld sleeves #8c5228 off region-rust.
Metalness 0.25, not physical: the thaikit harness has no environment map and a full metal renders black.
Textureless as DECLARED: a 256 px rust-bloom multiply canvas after construction (34 blooms per tile, ratio of #8c5228 over #b2c2c7 in linear space), one tile per metre of height, bump 0.02.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the medium class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: One component plus one repetition system: 2 of 4.

materials.note: steel only: 1 of 2; plate, bolt, nut and rust are vertex colours.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 1,120 of 2,000: eight boxes and six 6-seg bolt heads in the frame merge, and ten rung instances at 88 each (8-seg open rod, two 6-seg open sleeves, two 6-seg nuts).

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: Boxes for stiles, arms, gussets and plates; cylinders for rungs, sleeves, nuts and bolt heads.
One InstancedMesh of ten rungs. In a scene the HOST stacks the whole segment at 3.0 m steps.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.
The material is declared textureless. One 256 px rust-bloom canvas after construction, 0.25 MB of texture VRAM.

risks.description: The plate shows a two-rung short section; the proxy reads w/h 0.614 against the declared 0.233.
risks.mitigation: Built to the registry notes, which fix every station of the stacking contract; the plate supplies section, detail and materials. Residual and arithmetic recorded in envelopeDerivation and meshyNote.

risks.description: Every bay between rungs and stiles is background enclosed by the silhouette.
risks.mitigation: The turntable gate is run with --allow-holes on the _holecc measurement (enclosed components tens of px thick at every azimuth: real open bays, not tears).

risks.description: At 3.0 m tall and 0.70 wide the harness fit by bounding sphere crops the top and bottom of the turntable frames.
risks.mitigation: The crop is symmetric across azimuths, so the silhouette ratios the gate compares are unaffected; the hero is framed the same way for every tall prop in the kit.

risks.description: With the cage gone the ladder is a 0.26 m deep plane: edge-on at azimuth 90 and 270 its foreground covers 2.73% of the frame (measured on renders/beauty-090.png and -270.png against the #3a3a3a backdrop), under the turntable segmenter's 3.5% floor, so those two frames score 0.000 even with the declared collapse ratio 0.37 passed. Azimuth 0 and 180 cover 5.43% and 5.17% and score 1.000 and 0.947.
risks.mitigation: The same floor the 3 m fence panels sit under, and a genuine collapse would also fail 0/180, which pass; the 90/270 frames are read by eye instead (stile edge, two brackets at y 0.30, nothing else) and the FAIL is recorded here rather than worked around.

implementationRefinements.change: Rounded ten-segment rungs and weld collars; six separate steel washers beneath existing hex mounting bolts. Reduce overlarge 20mm rust bump to 3mm and use oxidized steel roughness. Retain the saved three-metre repeated ladder module, its single mounting level and tiling pitch.

Replace blurred brown blotches with reference-derived chipped paint and edge oxidation, mapped along stile length and rung circumference. Washers stay bare metal; module length, rung count and mounting contract retained.
Give steel stiles a physical 2 mm corner chamfer, and project the accepted chipped-paint crop onto the lower mounting plates. Keep bare bolt/washer geometry and all ten rungs.
